I need three puzzle inputs each with a unique solution. The simplest approach: a rectangle split into four wall-bounded regions, three colored and one empty, where the empty region touches all three colors so its fill is forced uniquely. I'm sketching a grid layout with a 2x2 arrangement of cells to make this work.

Testing the 2x2 quadrant idea, each region only borders two neighbors since diagonal cells don't touch through the wall cross, so that leaves the empty region ambiguous between two remaining colors. I need a layout where the empty region borders exactly three distinct colors — a stacked-column design where three colored regions sit in a column and one large empty region touches all three works better, forcing the fourth palette color uniquely.

Laying out grid rows and wall placements...

Still writing grid layout...

For the third pair, I'm considering a chain structure where an empty region touches three different colors, forcing its identity, then cascades to determine the rest uniquely.

I'm testing a left-column-of-three-regions layout with a middle empty region and a right empty region, but that setup fails to guarantee uniqueness since two colors could satisfy the constraints. I'll try adapting the earlier four-region layout instead, swapping which regions are colored versus empty.
